outcome: Every provider invocation reports what it actually cost and how it actually behaved - cache reuse, reasoning effort applied, and truncation - as normalized nullable facts that reach the operator surfaces and OpenTelemetry.

exclude: explicit cache-breakpoint control such as cache_control
a business or account-linked telemetry projection
cost or latency budgets and any threshold that fails a run

acceptance.text: Cache accounting already parsed from provider responses is surfaced rather than discarded, including OpenAI-style prompt cache hit and miss token counts and Bedrock-style cache read and write token counts.
The reasoning effort actually applied to an invocation is recorded alongside its token counts, distinguishing a value the profile requested from one the provider reported.
Every such fact is nullable with honest absence: a provider that reports no cache accounting yields an explicitly unavailable status, never a zero that reads as a measured result.
An invocation truncated by an output-token ceiling is reported as an explicit named failure carrying the provider's own finish reason, never as an empty successful result.

These facts are visible through the existing operator projection and are exported over OpenTelemetry using the same canonical values, so a run's cost and cache behaviour can be evaluated without reading provider logs.

constraints: Facts are nullable with honest absence; a missing provider fact never becomes zero.
Reuse the existing availability pattern on UsageReceipt rather than inventing a second shape for unavailable data.
One canonical projection feeds every operator surface; do not add a second telemetry path.
Measurement never becomes a gate: record the facts, fail no run on them.
